# API Architecture Plan

The Awtsmoos renews every request before transport can pretend to be the source;
Awtsmoos.com will keep one calm public contract while many small domain vessels carry the force.

## Evidence

The canonical Social Hub already composes focused API delegates. The separate Observatory still concentrates transport parsing, URL construction, 32 public methods, mutation bodies, route-health orchestration, and developer probes inside one `api.js`; its request factory is a second large switch. `feedTrending` exists in transport but is absent from the operation policy/groups/factory.

## Winning architecture

1. Preserve every current `socialApi` method and `{status, ok, body}` envelope.
2. Split transport into route covenant, query/form vessels, response parser, structured error, and one canonical transport.
3. Split methods into Core, Discovery, Feed, Profile, Relationship, Signal, Governance, Live, and Developer domain clients.
4. Compose those domains beneath one stable `SocialObservatoryApi` facade.
5. Replace operation arrays/switches with one immutable data-only registry.
6. Separate browser context adaptation (`BinahContextInputResolver`) from operation execution (`YesodOperationExecutor`).
7. Generate read/mutation policy, visible groups, execution, docs, and agent catalog from that registry.
8. Add a machine gateway that discovers freely, validates reads, and requires explicit `allowMutation: true` for mutations.
9. Preserve multi-group membership and existing group order.
10. Make `feedTrending` a first-class read operation.

## Safety and compatibility

Unknown operations fail closed. Mutation consequence text stays equivalent to the current policy. Server error payloads remain intact. Network failures and unreadable response bodies become structured client-side errors. Blank query values remain distinct from absent values. No generic agent route exposes filesystem, NodeOS, or migration mutation powers.

## Verification

Facade parity, exact route strings, query encoding, transport parsing, operation uniqueness, JSON-safe catalog, mutation classification, context adaptation, agent required-input errors, explicit mutation opt-in, existing Observatory tests, live route-health probes, and browser smoke.
